why: Yearly air passenger swings of -12.3% to +15.7% over five years, along with charge bands and strike indices, are believable figures for a low-cost airline's shortlist.
A car wash chain washing about 13,000 to 14,000 cars a day at roughly $12 a wash is believable, and profit equals revenue minus costs in both columns (4,953 - 4,316 = 637; 5,107 - 4,818 = 289).
All four pies add to 100%, and 1,350 respondents being 9% of customers implies about 15,000 home-delivery customers in the territory, which is believable for an online grocer.
Implied household incomes of about $1,600 to $23,000 at the basic rate, with PPP rates below basic rates, are believable for cheaper emerging markets.
Microfinance adding about 3.1 percentage points of GDP growth over a decade across five sectors is believable, and each bar's direct and indirect parts add to its note.
A dairy cooperative with about $430 million in revenue and product margins of 4% to 16% is believable.
A theatre producer with EUR 58 million in ticket sales, production costs at 71% and venue charges at 38% of revenue (so a loss) is believable.
All four student survey pies add to 100%, and samples of 990 and 1,280 are believable for college campuses.
A commercial broadcaster spending $549 million on programs is believable, and the eight items add exactly to the stated total.
A fast-growing, loss-making online tutoring startup with revenue of $24 million to $131 million and margins narrowing from -144% to -23% is believable for a venture-backed firm.
